items.title: TSD-RTS-25-002, Stage 2 ION Initial Business Case Preliminary Results
notes:
Matthew O'Neil, Manager, Rapid Transit Coordinate, provided a presentation on the preliminary results for the business case for Stage 2 ION. A copy of this presentation is attached to the agenda. He covered the potential options for Council's consideration, based on cost estimates and potential benefit, including a full Light Rail Transit (LRT) into Cambridge, partial LRT routes with different locations, and an express bus route. M. O'Neil provided that the LRT and BRT offer the greatest economic benefit, including in terms of cost-benefit ratio, and that the partial LRT route options do not achieve the economic and strategic goals to the same degree.

In reply to questions, Doug Spooner, Acting Commissioner, Transportation Services spoke to the funding requests being submitted to other levels of government for the major project and clarified area-rating practices for the Townships. He indicated that while some operational costs are area-rated, the degree to which capital costs, if at all, are to be area-rated needs to be investigated. D. Spooner added that the rural transit strategy is about to see a funding support request to the province to initiate progress.

Responding to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner spoke to how the business plan relates to diversified ridership, especially as it pertains to student ridership. 

Replying to a question from the Committee, M. O'Neil provided clarification on the timeline going forward, indicating there is a great emphasis on the report expected for November, which may dictate much of what is to come for the future of the project. Additionally, he answered that the benefits come primarily from the switch to transit more broadly. 

Responding to a question from the Committee, M. O'Neil spoke to constraints around the Delta station that contribute to it being a less viable option than others being presented. In addition, he provided further information on ridership projections based on Stage 1 projections being met. N. Malcolm elaborated on the success of the frequent transit network in relation to the rapist transit system and spoke to the question of express buses to the ION, indicating this is being considered.

Staff indicated that a policy regarding lane designations can be explored, related to usage by bikes, mobility devices, and other vehicles.

Received for information.

items.title: PDL-AIR-25-004, Airport Growth Plan Update
notes:
Rod Regier, Commissioner, Planning, Development, and Legislative Services, provided an introduction to the report, highlighting the major changes made to the airport. Chris Wood, Director, Region of Waterloo International Airport, provided a presentation on the airport growth plan. A copy of this presentation is attached to the agenda. He outlined the key themes of the growth plan and spoke to the launching of phase 2 of the public consultation plan. C. Wood provided the strategic advantage of the airport, including as an economic impact tool. He elaborated on the potential passenger growth based on existing information and projected trends. He emphasized the need to preserve the cultural and natural heritage in the area when considering any modifications or improvements to the airport.

In reply to a question from the Committee, C. Wood provided a background on the previous site for the airport.

Responding to a question from the Committee, C. Wood expanded on the process for the recovery of costs. He added that the airport does do private and semi-private chartered flights.

Received for information.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
TSD-TRP-25-014, Municipal Speed Camera Program - Mid Year Update
notes:
D. Spooner provided an introduction to the report and presentation, highlighting the success of the pilot program. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. He elaborated on the rationale behind the Automated Speed Enforcement (ASE) program, and the findings behind the research that show its efficacy. Theresa Mendler, Manager, Processing Centre (Automated Enforcement), spoke to compliance and speed data. Kaileigh Pfaff, Supervisor, Administrative Penalties Program, spoke to the data on tickets and payment, as well as the operating details for the program. T. Mendler spoke to excessive speeding cases that underlie the concerns raised with speeding in school zones. D. Spooner discussed the media campaigns underway for road safety programs.

In response to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner clarified the key difference in licensing for drivers as it relates to ASE, which is operated solely by the Ministry of Transportation (MTO). He added that the Region is also addressing the issue of potential insurance impacts related to ASE for employees of the Region.

Replying to questions from the Committee, D. Spooner clarified that staff cannot predict when school areas will be utilized, but if directed, will make that recommendation. He further spoke to the potential financial hardships and indicated staff is cognizant of them, noting the one-time offences that suggest there are not too many repeat offenders. D. Spooner indicated staff can look into further human engagement for the appeal process.

Responding to a question from the Committee, D. Sponer explained that there are jurisdictions which do fines based on income, but that staff are looking at appealed tickets through the lens of who is able to pay. In addition, D. Spooner clarified that lots of inquiries currently revolve around more speed cameras, and reiterated that there are other programs in place to discourage speeding in areas which are not eligible for ASE.

Replying to a question, T. Mendler indicated there are plans for more speed cameras in the City of Waterloo, anticipated for 2026.

Responding to questions, D. Spooner and T. Mendler elaborated on the public education campaign, and clarified the delivery of the informational brochures.

In reply to questions from the Committee, D. Spooner explained the follow-up to be had with Waterloo Regional Police Service in terms of the more serious stunt driving instances and ways to enforce. D. Spooner clarified that vandalism costs are covered by the contractors, and indicated the Region is lower to comparators such as Toronto. He further explained why the number of tickets issued does not equal the number of instances of speeding, due to errors and administrative factors.

Replying to questions, D. Spooner clarified the usage and design of the road safety reserves, and confirmed a report is expected for later this year which discusses road safety reserves. He further elaborated on methods of intervening to decrease speeding. There is an additional report coming on the rural road safety strategy, and a third report to consider revenue-sharing with area municipalities.

Responding to a question from the Committee, D. Sooner indicated that if there were legislative changes to ASE, there would be cancellation costs to the Region, as well as other impacts.

Received for information.

motions.text: Th at the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the expropriation of lands for Phase 1 of improvements to Lancaster Street West (Regional Road 29) between Bridgeport Road East and Elizabeth Street, in the City of Kitchener, in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo , as detailed in Report PDL-LEG- 25 - 030 , dated September 9 , 202 5 , described as follows: Fee Simple Partial Bridgeport Road East and Elizabeth Street, and all related improvements, and works ancillary thereto and for such purposes, the free, unimpeded and unobstructed access to the lands at all times by motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the expropriation of lands for Phase 1 of improvements to Lancaster Street West (Regional Road 29) between Bridgeport Road East and Elizabeth Street, in the City of Kitchener, in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, as detailed in Report PDL-LEG-25-030, dated September 9, 2025, described as follows:

Fee Simple Partial Taking:

  1. Part of Lot 25, Plan 789, being Part 3 on 58R-22144, City of Kitchener, part of PIN 22340-0221, (405 Lancaster Street West, City of Kitchener)
  2. Part of Lot 20, Plan 666, being Part 3 on 58R-22143, City of Kitchener, part of PIN 22304-0003 (392 Lancaster Street West, City of Kitchener)
  3. Part of Lot 21, Plan 789, being Part 2 on 58R-22143, City of Kitchener, part of PIN 22339-0104 (383 Lancaster Street West, City of Kitchener)

Temporary Easement – Grading:

The right and easement, being a temporary easement in gross, for the free and unobstructed, right, interest and easement terminating, for the subject properties set out below, on the 31st day of December, 2027, for itself, its successors and assigns, and anyone authorized by it, on, over, under and through the following property for the purposes of excavation, construction, installation, replacement, alteration, grading, and landscaping as required in connection with the improvements to Lancaster Street West between Bridgeport Road East and Elizabeth Street, and all related improvements, and works ancillary thereto and for such purposes, the free, unimpeded and unobstructed access to the lands at all times by employees, agents, contractors, workers and anyone authorized by it, and vehicles, supplies and equipment at all times and for all purposes and things necessary for or incidental to the exercise and enjoyment of the right and easement:

  1. Part of Lot 25, Plan 789, being Part 2 on 58R-22144, City of Kitchener, part of PIN 22340-0221, (405 Lancaster Street West, City of Kitchener)
  2. Part of Lot 21, Plan 789, being Part 1 on 58R-22143, City of Kitchener, part of PIN 22339-0104 (383 Lancaster Street West, City of Kitchener)

And that staff be instructed to register a Plan of Expropriation for the properties within three months of the granting of the approval to expropriate the properties, as required by the Expropriations Act;

And that the registered owners be served with a Notice of Expropriation, Notice of Election and a Notice of Possession for the properties after the registration of the Plan of Expropriation and the Regional Solicitor is authorized to take any and all actions required to enforce such Notices including but not limited to any application pursuant to Section 40 of the Expropriations Act;

And that the Regional Solicitor is authorized to enter into an agreement with the registered owners, or to make an application under Section 39 of the Expropriations Act, to adjust the date for possession specified in the Notice of Possession as may be required;

And that all above-referenced fee simple partial takings situated adjacent to an existing Regional public highway be acquired for road widening purposes and therefore be deemed to form part of the adjacent public highway in accordance with subsection 31(6) of the Municipal Act, 2001;

And that if no agreement as to compensation is made with an owner, the statutory Offer of Compensation and payment be served upon the registered owners of the properties in the amount of the market value of the interests in the land as estimated by the Region’s appraiser in accordance with the Expropriations Act;

And that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to execute any Indemnity agreement or other document related to payment of the statutory Offer of Compensation;

And further that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to discontinue expropriation proceedings or any part thereof, in respect of the above described lands, or any part thereof, upon the registration on title of the required documentation to complete the transaction or if determined by the Commissioner, Engineering & Environmental Services, that such lands, or any part or interest thereof, are not required for the subject Project.
